sourceClaims: Foundational programs remain while complementary training is integrated around goals and constraints.
Source #85 describes meaningful repeated program learning, not random introductions to every movement.
Source #123 specifically discusses shorter lower-weight maintenance when adding conventional lifting; it does not prescribe this app algorithm.
appAdaptations: Capacity-triggered focused development, earned maintenance and queued selections derive from actual current-method history. Actual plans retain scheduling intent; no new configuration field or mutable curriculum phase is added.
Half-volume whole-unit rounding, or one familiar set in short sessions, is a nonadvancing earned-maintenance choice. The familiar owned working load is retained; no lower weight is invented.
Wave/row-wave methods are excluded from the new reduction. All unearned targets, intervals and existing recovery/technical/equipment gates remain intact.
A new full endpoint is required after earned-maintenance light work before further progression review.
At most two earned maintenance additions, and at most four movements after additions, must fit the selected time ceiling.
Primary program days and maintenance pending queues use separate written ownership; no extra program-day, component or forecast credit is inferred.
limits: No universal source maintenance frequency, numerical reservation formula or clinically validated minimum maintenance dose is claimed.
Thirty-minute capacity may queue later skills rather than introduce them all; queueing is an explicit breadth-versus-earned-cycle tradeoff.
Historical physical technique, real strength retention and Android acceptance still require separate verification.
All ten Wildman gate areas remain unresolved.
